questions.text:
Wāhanga Tuatahi / Section One: He reta ki te Poari — A letter to the Board of Trustees

A group of rangatahi at Te Uenuku College have decided to write to their Board of Trustees to ask for the establishment of a head boy Māori (Amokura Tāne) and a head girl Māori (Amokura Wahine). Senior Māori students Te Atarauhina and Māwhai discuss the plan via text messages. They discuss reasons for having Māori head students, including visibility (kanohi kitea), being role models (kaikawe), and advocating for te reo Māori in the school. Māwhai raises concerns about the name 'Amokura' vs 'prefect' and whether there are strategies for te reo in the school.

Pātai Tuatahi / Question One:
Kei te tuhi a Te Atarauhina tētahi reta ki te Poari o te kura kia tono mō tētahi Amokura Wahine me tētahi Amokura Tāne. He aha ōu whakaaro? Kei te whakaae, whakahē rānei? He aha ai?

Te Atarauhina is to write to the Board of Trustees to ask for the establishment of a Māori head boy and a Māori head girl. Do you agree or disagree? Explain your reason, using evidence from the text.

Write your answer in te reo Māori OR English.
questions.markingGuide:
Achieved (Paetae 3-4): States if they agree or disagree and provides a basic reason why. Provides minimal links to the text.

Merit (Kaiaka 5-6): Provides a detailed description of why they agree or disagree. Offers detailed ideas linking back to the text. Provides the beginning of a detailed link to the text.

Excellence (Kairangi 7-8): Provides a well-crafted description of why they agree or disagree with Te Atarauhina's idea. Expands on their detailed opinion using relevant evidence from the text. Links ideas and includes personal reflections. Shows understanding of the meaning and purpose of the text. May discuss concepts such as: visibility and representation of Māori students; the role of kaikawe (advocates) for te reo; the importance of using Māori terms like Amokura rather than 'prefect'; how Māori leadership benefits the whole school community.

questions.text:
Pātai Tuarua / Question Two:
Ko ngā mahi a Te Atarauhina hei waihotanga mā te kura. Ko tāu mahi te tuhi he rautaki hei whakamahinga i tō kura.

Te Atarauhina has paved the way for future students of her Kura. How would you use the ideas of Te Atarauhina within your Kura?

Write your answer in te reo Māori OR English.
questions.markingGuide:
Achieved (Paetae 3-4): Provides a limited description of what they would do with Te Atarauhina's ideas in their school. States whether they like them. Attempts to explain how they will use Te Atarauhina's ideas in their kura.

Merit (Kaiaka 5-6): Provides a more detailed description of Te Atarauhina's ideas and why they like them. Discusses how they will use them in their own school. Some personal reflections and ideas linking back to text.

Excellence (Kairangi 7-8): Provides a well-developed and detailed description of Te Atarauhina's ideas and why they like them. Explains with well-developed ideas how they would use them in their school. Links ideas to the text, including personal reflections. Shows understanding of the meaning and purpose of, and the reason for, the text. May discuss: establishing Māori leadership roles; promoting kapa haka, te reo classes, and cultural activities; ensuring Māori voices are heard in school governance.

questions.text:
Pātai Tuatoru / Question Three:
You have been elected as Deputy Head Student to Te Atarauhina. Your task is to help write a plan that supports achieving the goals outlined by Te Atarauhina in her speech. Identify the order of priority for these goals and explain why you have selected this order.

The goals discussed include: establishing a kapa haka group, bringing mātanga (experts) to teach workshops in te toi (arts), kapa haka, te wharepora (weaving), and other areas; having kanohi kitea (visible Māori presence); being kaikawe (advocates) who speak to the Tumuaki (principal) and the Board.

Write your answer in te reo Māori OR English.
questions.markingGuide:
Achieved (Paetae 3-4): Provides a limited description of the plan they would create. Brief description of how they would carry out their plan. Provides limited links to the text.

Merit (Kaiaka 5-6): Provides details of their plan and how they would prioritise their tasks. Explains an opinion of why they have ordered/prioritised their task list. Limited personal reflections and ideas linking back to the text.

Excellence (Kairangi 7-8): Provides insights into their plan and it is well detailed. Suggests clearly why they have ordered/prioritised their task list. Links ideas to the text, including personal reflections. Shows understanding of the meaning and purpose of the text. May discuss: prioritising kanohi kitea first to build visibility; setting up kapa haka to engage students; then advocating to the Board for structural changes; the whakataukī 'Ina noho takitini i runga i te whakaaro kotahi ka ea, ka tutuki' (when many stand as one on the same idea, it will be achieved).
